rationale: bugs_open/445 was filed as 'the layout library has no archetype for content-hub-with-embedded-tools, so three briefs converged on magazine-grid'. That is true and it is a symptom. The mechanism is that the estate cannot SEE a library gap of that shape, by construction. site-design-planner's library-growth signal (needs_new_layout_candidate) is emitted only when resolveLayoutByTags returns IsFallback (no layout scores above zero anywhere in the library) or IsSchemeMismatch. But the category (0.75), description (<=0.90) and same-scheme (0.50) bonuses are added to `total` INDEPENDENTLY of any tag matching, so `total > 0` is satisfiable with `tagScore == 0`. A layout matching NONE of a site's tags therefore counts as the library having answered, and no gap is recorded. MEASURED 2026-09-03: four live sites are recorded by this very code as `tags 0.00` WITH lineage layout_source `library_match`; exactly TWO needs_new_layout_candidate items exist across 63,007 work items ever written (29,657 live UNION 33,350 archived), and BOTH are from the degenerate no-tags-at-all arm — so the number of times this mechanism has assessed the library and reported it short is zero. Meanwhile the classifier's live prompt tells the model 'an unmatched tag will trigger a library-growth review work item rather than silently fail', which is false. This change does not invent a mechanism: migration 103_site_design_planner.sql specified it in April 2026 (lineage.layout_match_score '(float 0-1) — tag-overlap score for chosen layout', a threshold whose worked example reads 'above threshold 0.5', and layout_source 'needs_new_layout_candidate') and none of the three was ever built. It computes the normalised score, records it with the threshold in force, and widens the predicate to fire on weak tag fit. SELECTION IS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED — no site's layout moves; only what is recorded and whether a parked review item is filed. The threshold 0.50 is taken from the measured coverage distribution's widest empty band (38%-62%) rather than invented; the only other empty band (10%-15%) is about one tag wide on a ten-term site and would flip on ordinary classifier variance. What I most want challenged: (a) whether firing on weak fit will flood a queue nobody drains — my answer is that the durable record is the resolved_composition row and the work item is site-scoped and deduped by item_key, with clustering planned as a separate fleet sweep; (b) whether promoting lineage.layout_source to 'needs_new_layout_candidate' on a gap loses the information that a real library_match occurred — I keep layout_gap_flagged/layout_gap_reason as separate keys and leave library_fallback intact for the fallback arm, but a reviewer may prefer the enum untouched; (c) whether the coverage denominator should include terms no layout carries (it does, deliberately — a term the library cannot serve is exactly what must count against fit).

edits.rationale: Add lmMinTagCoverage tunable plus layoutFit struct and LibraryGap()/GapReason() methods, so the gap predicate has ONE definition shared by the action and its tests and cannot drift.

Compute the fit inside resolveLayoutByTags using the caller's OWN idf weight closure, so the coverage numerator and denominator are guaranteed to use identical weights. Recomputing them separately is how two halves of a ratio silently stop being comparable.
fallbackLayout gains siteTerms so a fallback records coverage 0 with EVERY term listed as unmatched. Left as a zero value, an absent fit and a measured-zero fit read identically downstream.
edits.sketch: func fallbackLayout(..., siteTerms map[string]struct{}, logger) { fit := layoutFit{SiteTermCount: len(siteTerms), UnmatchedTerms: lmKeys(siteTerms), Threshold: lmMinTagCoverage} ... IsWeakFit: len(siteTerms) > 0 }

edits.rationale: Widen the emit condition from `IsFallback || IsSchemeMismatch` to resolution.LibraryGap(), add a weak-fit warn branch, and report `source` on EVERY branch (previously only the theme-kit one, which forced the installer to infer layout_source from is_fallback — an inference that cannot represent a scheme gap or a weak fit).

Carry the fit into the work item's spec AND its summary. The percentage goes in the summary so a reviewer can triage the queue by number without opening each row, and so a cluster of sites leaning on the same thin match is visible as a pattern in a list view. unmatched_terms is the operative field: it distinguishes 'we need a new layout for this shape' from 'an existing layout needs these tags'.
